around.headline: Bus stop query turns bloody: man robbed of ₹25,000, stabbed in Bengaluru
around.summary: A man was stabbed and robbed of ₹25,000 after a stranger who approached him with a casual query at a bus stop turned violent. If someone corners you with a weapon out, comply and hand over valuables immediately — no phone or cash is worth resisting an armed robber.

around.headline: Spam calls are graduating to e-SIM fraud, Bengaluru police warn
around.summary: Police flagged a shift from routine spam/OTP calls toward more sophisticated e-SIM swap fraud, where scammers trick victims into authorising a SIM transfer that then lets them intercept banking OTPs. Never approve a SIM-swap or e-SIM request with your telecom provider that you didn't personally initiate.

around.headline: Two more on-duty Bengaluru officials assaulted in a single day
around.summary: A woman police sub-inspector was assaulted and body-shamed while breaking up a quarrel, and separately a JD(S) functionary allegedly assaulted a traffic cop on duty — the third such assault on an officer reported in the city in two days. Assaulting on-duty police is a non-bailable offence, not a roadside dispute to shrug off.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The Times of India

around.headline: Toddler critical after falling from third floor of Bengaluru home
around.summary: A 2-year-old is fighting for life after falling from the third floor of a residential building in the city. If you have young children at home, check today that balcony grilles, window locks and gaps under railings are actually childproofed, not just assumed safe since move-in.

around.headline: BMTC adds 62 daily trips on Magadi Road with new express service
around.summary: BMTC has added 62 daily trips on the Magadi Road corridor via a new express service, aimed at easing the crunch on one of the city's busier commuter routes. Worth checking the new express timings if you travel this stretch regularly.

around.headline: Maruthi Sevanagar flyover finally gets off the ground after years of delay
around.summary: Construction on the long-stalled Maruthi Sevanagar flyover has finally begun after years of delay. Expect construction-related detours and slower traffic near the site as work ramps up.

around.headline: India opens tax amnesty scheme for small taxpayers with undisclosed foreign assets
around.summary: The central government has opened a tax amnesty window letting small taxpayers declare previously undisclosed foreign assets without the usual penalties. If this applies to you, it's worth reviewing the scheme's terms before the window closes rather than continuing to sit on undisclosed holdings.

street_smart.title: A stranger at a quiet bus stop asks you something simple — the time, directions — then doesn't walk away and stays close. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident today: a man was robbed of ₹25,000 and stabbed in Bengaluru after a casual query at a bus stop turned violent (The Times of India). Nearly every evergreen rotation topic (digital-arrest scams, UPI fraud, auto/cab overcharging, rental/tenant traps, fake job offers, OTP scams, two-wheeler theft, medical emergencies, consumer court, phone snatching, loan-app harassment, credit-card skimming) has run within the last three weeks, so this news-based scenario is used instead.
street_smart.situation: Moments after the stranger lingers, he flashes a blade and demands your phone and cash — and you have to decide what to do in the next few seconds.

choices.text: Refuse and grab for your phone or pocket to protect your belongings, trying to push past him.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Resisting a weapon-armed robber over a phone or cash is exactly how today's case ended in a stabbing — no possession is worth escalating a knife confrontation.

choices.text: Comply immediately — hand over the phone and cash without sudden movements, then move to a lit, populated place and call 100 once you're safe.
choices.feedback: Correct. Safety over property is the rule whenever a weapon is shown. Complying fast minimizes the risk of physical harm; report immediately afterward, including your phone's IMEI, so it can be blocked and traced.

choices.text: Try to talk him down or negotiate keeping some of the cash while handing over the phone.
choices.feedback: Negotiating buys you nothing but time, and it invites unpredictability from someone who has already shown a weapon. Comply fully and quickly instead of bargaining.

choices.text: Scream and try to attract a crowd's attention without handing anything over yet.
choices.feedback: This can work in a busy, well-lit area, but it's a gamble at a quiet, empty bus stop after dark — it can provoke faster violence before any help actually arrives.

takeaways: If a weapon is shown, comply first — no phone or cash is worth a stab wound; safety beats property every time.
Right after, call 100 and note the direction the attacker fled; use your phone's IMEI (dial *#06# in advance and save it) to get your telecom operator to blacklist a stolen handset.
Where possible, avoid standing alone at isolated, dimly lit bus stops after dark — waiting near a shop or a cluster of other commuters cuts the odds of being singled out.

quiz.question: BMTC has added how many daily trips on the Magadi Road corridor with its new express service?
quiz.why: The express service is aimed at easing crowding on one of the city's busiest commuter corridors.

quiz.question: Bengaluru police flagged a scam trend where spam calls are now graduating into what kind of fraud?
quiz.why: An e-SIM swap can let a fraudster hijack your phone number and intercept the OTPs your bank sends for verification.

quiz.question: Aspirants protesting a JPSC-JSSC recruitment exam row burned effigies of which leaders?
options: Hemant Soren, Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav
Narendra Modi, Amit Shah and Nitish Kumar
Mamata Banerjee, Yogi Adityanath and Devendra Fadnavis
M K Stalin, Pinarayi Vijayan and Siddaramaiah
quiz.why: The protest is over Jharkhand's public service exam recruitment process, with aspirants threatening to lay siege to the CM's residence.

quiz.question: The Cauvery river, long at the centre of an interstate water-sharing dispute, originates in which state?
quiz.why: It rises at Talakaveri in Kodagu district and flows through Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry before reaching the Bay of Bengal.

quiz.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution abolished untouchability?
quiz.why: Article 17 falls under the Right against Exploitation and makes practising untouchability in any form a punishable offence.
